newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Anzoil agrees Vietnam gas deal.
newsitem.headline: Anzoil agrees Vietnam gas deal.

text.p: Anzoil NL said on Wednesday that Electricity Vietnam had executed a memorandum of understanding confirming that it wishes to buy gas from the D14 Song Tra Ly gasfield in the onshore Hanoi Basin.

The average daily gas usage specified by Electricity Vietnam is 8.472 million cubic feet per day over a minimum of 10 years commencing at the beginning of the second quarter 1998, Anzoil said. Electricity Vietnam owns the 35 megawat Tien Hai gas-fired power station, located seven km from the gasfield.
Anzoil said in its weekly drilling report that D14-STL-3 was flowing gas and fracture fluid at an unmeasured rate and D14-STL-lx was flowing gas at a rate too small to measure.
"Static pressure surveys will be run in both wells to determine the fluid level and composition inside the tubing which may be restricting the well performance," Anzoil said.
Anzoil, through its wholly-owned subsidiary Anzoil (Asia) Pte Ltd, holds a majority interest for the production sharing contract for the Hanoi Basin and is operator.
Frontier Petroleum NL holds a minority interest.
Their stakes were originally 80/20 but they are now in dispute over their respective holdings since Frontier failed to meet a drawdown notice in February.
